clue.text: Erase recording of hit, except for introduction

indicators.note: the word for hit loses its opening letter, the part that introduces it

parts.note: to swipe is to hit with a sweeping blow

explanation.surface: An instruction to delete a recording of some hit, keeping only its opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except for introduction' takes the S off SWIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe a tape or disc is to erase what has been recorded on it.

clue.text: World's top performer given some coverage?

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: a rapper is a hip-hop performer

explanation.surface: The world's leading performer gets a bit of press coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' takes W, the first letter of World's; 'coverage' is literal, a wrapper being a covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapper is a covering for something, hence some coverage, with the question mark flagging the pun.

clue.text: Promoted glass salesman's accepted on staff

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the word on goes inside
in a down clue, promoted means raised, so the words glass and salesman are read bottom to top

parts.note: a lens is a piece of shaped glass
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A glass salesman, promoted, has been taken on to the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promoted' turns both words upward in this down entry, giving PERSNEL; 'accepted' takes ON inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Personnel are the people employed by an organisation, its workforce.

clue.text: Banned player did not appear to defend personal assault

parts.note: a pro is a professional player

indicators.note: to defend is to surround and protect, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: hid means kept out of sight
a bite is an attack on someone's person

explanation.surface: A banned sportsman stayed away rather than defend himself against an assault charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defend' signals one piece wrapped round another, guarding it; a bite counts as an assault on someone's person.
explanation.definitionFit: Prohibited means forbidden, a direct synonym of banned.

clue.text: Tell uplifting story in bible class?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting means raising, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: An inspiring story told in Sunday school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns TALE to ELAT, which goes 'in' RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or narrate it.

clue.text: Small number coming in excited about film

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: high means excited or elated
on means concerning, about
no is the short form of number

explanation.surface: A small number of people come in, thrilled about a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' puts the short number inside the phrase for excited about, splitting it.
explanation.definitionFit: High Noon is the 1952 Western starring Gary Cooper.

clue.text: Attempt to recruit north German writer to lead MA course

indicators.note: to recruit is to take in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a bash is a go or attempt

indicators.note: to lead means to go in front, so the writer comes before the letters MA

parts.note: George Sand was the French novelist

explanation.surface: An attempt to enlist a northern German writer to run a master's course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recruit' takes everything from north to MA inside the attempt; 'course' is part of a meal, not a degree course. George Sand was a French novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausages with mashed potato make a familiar British main course of a meal.

clue.text: Tax cut about to be introduced — a small one

indicators.note: introduced means put inside, so the letter goes into the other piece
cut means shortened, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a tithe is a levy of a tenth
C stands for circa, about

explanation.surface: A tax cut is about to come in, but only a little one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks TITHE to TITH; C is 'introduced' to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Titch is British slang for a small person, a little one.

clue.text: Court's upholding urgent orders

indicators.note: in a down clue, upholding means sitting below and supporting, so the court comes last

parts.note: dire can mean urgent or desperate
Ct is the abbreviation for court, plus S

explanation.surface: A court upholds some urgent orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upholding' works because this is a down entry: the court sits underneath and holds the other word up.
explanation.definitionFit: Directs as a verb means instructs or commands, so it matches orders.

clue.text: Eggheads: popular TV broadcast with men reaching final every now and then

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: telly is British slang for television
gents are men

indicators.note: every now and then picks out alternate letters

explanation.surface: Eggheads on a popular TV programme, with the men occasionally reaching the final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' gives TELLI by sound from TELLY; 'every now and then' takes IA from final.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggheads is slang for intellectuals, the cultured class that forms a nation's thinkers.

clue.text: A doctor taking course about a particular gland

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lane is a course on a running track or pool

explanation.surface: A doctor takes a course on a specific gland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns LANE to ENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The adrenal is one specific gland, sitting above each kidney.

clue.text: Pop singer not the first to fail

indicators.note: to fail is to go wrong, so the letters break down and rearrange
the opening letter of the word singer is dropped

explanation.surface: A pop singer who failed to come first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' leaves INGER; with TO, 'fail' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is an informal word for father, and a genitor is a natural father.

clue.text: Re-issued threat to inspect worker's attitude

indicators.note: something reissued is put out again in new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A renewed threat to inspect someone's approach to their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Re-issued' rearranges all fifteen letters of threat to inspect.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the belief that hard work and thrift are moral duties, an outlook on labour.

clue.text: Halfway through therapy, part of body found to keep hurting

indicators.note: halfway through picks the letter at the midpoint of the word therapy

parts.note: the ankle is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Midway through physiotherapy, a body part is found to be still painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halfway through' gives R, the fourth of the seven letters of therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to cause lasting resentment or pain, to go on hurting.

clue.text: Twice Northerner ignores tips for making dish

indicators.note: twice means the remaining piece appears two times
the tips are the two end letters, which are left out

parts.note: a Scouse is a Liverpudlian, from the north of England

explanation.surface: A northerner twice turns down tips while making a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignores tips' trims SCOUSE to COUS; 'Twice' doubles it. Scouse is the speech and people of Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Couscous is a North African dish of steamed semolina grains.

clue.text: Hand over key — I'm going

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the letters of I'm depart from the front of the word for key

parts.note: imperative means vital or crucial, key
the two letters of I'm, which leave the word

explanation.surface: Handing over the key as someone leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm going' takes IM off IMPERATIVE, leaving PERATIVE. 'Hand' is a worker, not the act of handing.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory hand is a manual worker, which is what an operative is.

clue.text: Challenging attitude of French partner

parts.note: de is French for of
a fiancé is a partner engaged to be married

explanation.surface: A French partner is in a challenging mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance, a bold confrontational stance.

clue.text: Abused in a queue perhaps on motorway

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: M is used for motorway, as in M1
people standing in a queue are lined up, in line

explanation.surface: Drivers stuck in a motorway tailback get abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts ALIGNED after M.
explanation.definitionFit: Maligned means slandered or spoken ill of, a form of verbal abuse.

clue.text: I'm heading northwards, crossing American state such as Oklahoma!

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so one piece straddles the other
in a down clue, heading north means the letters run upwards

parts.note: taken as written, minus the apostrophe
Cal is the abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: Someone driving north across an American state, Oklahoma for one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading northwards' turns IM to MI; MI 'crossing' US gives MUSI. Oklahoma looks like the state, but it is the Rodgers and Hammerstein show.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma! is a famous stage show with songs, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Name of upper-class girl revealed in articles

indicators.note: revealed in means found inside, so one piece goes within the others

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a is the other indefinite article
gel mimics a posh pronunciation of girl

explanation.surface: The name of a posh girl comes out in newspaper articles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' gives both indefinite articles; 'gel' is a mocking spelling of a posh pronunciation of girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Notice groom making speech

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
to dress hair or a horse is to groom it

explanation.surface: A notice that the groom will give a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal talk delivered to an audience.

clue.text: Accountant raised very little money, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
a cent is a coin of tiny value

explanation.surface: An accountant raised hardly any money, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns CA to AC; 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a stock phrase but its last four words are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is a characteristic way of pronouncing words, a style of speech.

clue.text: Tory faces uproar, installed in post as deputy leader

indicators.note: installed in means placed inside, so these pieces go within the other

parts.note: to send a letter is to post it

indicators.note: faces means stands in front of, so the Tory comes before the uproar

parts.note: con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
din is a loud noise or uproar
the punctuation mark itself is a comma

explanation.surface: A Conservative faces an outcry after being given a job as the party's number two.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after uproar is not punctuation: it is a piece of wordplay, the word COMMA. The surface reads 'post' as a job; here it means to mail, which is to send.
explanation.definitionFit: A second in command is the officer next below the chief, the deputy to the leader.

clue.text: You can get tea in several supermarkets

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Tea is on sale in many supermarkets.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of supermarkets under one owner forms a retail chain.

clue.text: Chinese solver's on song

parts.note: Charlie Chan is the fictional Chinese detective, a solver of crimes, plus S

explanation.surface: A Chinese crossword solver goes on about a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver is a crime-solver: Charlie Chan, detective of novels and films.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanson is the French word for a song, used in English for a French cabaret song.

clue.text: See unit fixed in adjoining bathroom

indicators.note: fixed means repaired or rearranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Look at the unit fitted in the bathroom next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges SEEUNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An en suite is a private bathroom directly joined to a bedroom.

clue.text: Fast time? Final part of hymn, note, to be played in slow time

definitions.text: to be played in slow time

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
amen is sung at the end of a hymn
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A Lenten hymn with a closing note to be sung slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' is abstaining from food, not speed, which sets up the contrast with slow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentamente is the Italian musical direction meaning slowly.

clue.text: Eating place sometimes serving sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the answer lies within the words sometimes serving

explanation.surface: A café that occasionally serves sandwiches.
